7.note: sep-CMA-ES pilot on gtbench kuhn_poker (PLAN.md training recipe step 2, 'Validate the loop first on gtbench's cheap kuhn_poker before spending chess GPU-hours on it'). Code written this session (cloud dev routine, no GPU/gtbench access to actually run it): src/open_fugu/train/train_cmaes.py (generic sep-CMA-ES trainer -- flatten_params/unflatten_params/run_cmaes, pure numpy + the cma package, no torch dependency at all), src/open_fugu/gtbench_ext/{local_transformers_model,orchestrator_router_model}.py (GTBench-compatible Model wrappers -- one local worker, one real per-query Fugu-routed dispatcher over a small worker pool, same argmax-over-backbone-logits design a2a/orchestrator_agent.py.FuguSelectionDispatch uses for chess), scripts/phase7_setup_gtbench.sh (idempotent vendor/gtbench clone -- jinhaoduan/GTBench -- plus pyspiel/python-box install via uv), scripts/phase7_cmaes_kuhn_pilot.py (the pilot itself: evolves the selection head weight+bias against real kuhn_poker win/loss/draw reward vs. a fixed RandomAgent baseline). advance_phase_7 registered in orchestrate.py, dry-run-verified (mocked tmux) to gate/launch/complete correctly. Unlike a plain py_compile check, this was verified much more thoroughly than usual for a GPU-blocked phase: the cloud sandbox has outbound network access, so this session actually git-cloned the real jinhaoduan/GTBench upstream, installed pyspiel+cma+numpy into a throwaway venv, and ran the REAL gtbench game loop (KuhnPoker, PromptAgent, RandomAgent, HistoryTracker) end-to-end with fake/mock LLM models standing in for the real GPU-backed ones -- confirmed the model.query() interface contract, the winner-name reward-extraction logic, and (via a mock torch shim) OrchestratorRouterModel's argmax routing + selection-head weight-loading all work correctly. Also found and fixed a real upstream landmine this way: vendor/gtbench/gamingbench/games/__init__.py eagerly imports every game module, which transitively imports gamingbench/chat/chat.py, which does a bare top-level unconditional 'from langchain.chat_models import ...' -- installing real langchain risked pydantic-version conflicts with this project's already-pinned torch/transformers/a2a-sdk stack, so gtbench_ext/_langchain_stub/ provides minimal same-named stub modules instead (verified working against the real GTBench clone). train_cmaes.run_cmaes itself was also verified against a real cma installation (toy sphere-function fitness, confirmed it actually converges). Only genuinely unverifiable-from-here pieces: real torch/GPU tensor ops and actual worker-LLM inference (models/local_worker.py, already used by Phase 3-5). Gated behind gpu_spend_approved (false by default, same pattern as Phase 3/5) since PLAN.md's own estimate is 2-5 days of real GPU-hours across many CMA-ES generations -- independent of Phase 0.5's chess-quality REVIEW_NEEDED verdict (kuhn_poker doesn't depend on chess skill at all), but still a nontrivial autonomous multi-day spend a human should sign off on first. See STATUS.md.
